goals: mechanistic: resolve how elevation (via orographic forcing + snow) and soil texture control water partitioning across the Upper Yakima
validation: compare simulated peak SWE against in-domain SNOTEL; assess streamflow only if routing is added
key_processes: ET vs runoff vs drainage partitioning

model_choice.rationale: Single-column ELM across a real heterogeneous HUC8; NLDAS-2 supplies elevation-varying forcing over the 1900 m relief and simulates SWE for SNOTEL validation.

answerable: elevation control on partitioning to the ~12 km NLDAS granularity (orographic precip/temperature gradient varies with column elevation)
snow accumulation / peak SWE and its elevation dependence (H2OSNO/SWE in default output)
soil-texture control on partitioning via per-column SSURGO

not_answerable.aspect: sub-12 km elevation contrasts (ridgetop vs valley finer than a NLDAS cell)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS has no within-cell lapse rate; sub-12 km terrain unresolved, ridgetop SWE biased low
single-column ELM has no lateral routing; no native integrated streamflow

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil), oversampled at rain-snow transition
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 5 elevation bands span the 1900 m relief at roughly the granularity NLDAS can distinguish; crossing with 2 dominant soils (10) prevents elevation/soil confounding; +1 extra column in the rain-snow transition band for light replication where snow-season partitioning is most sensitive.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Distribute across the 5 bands following the DEM hypsometry; oversample the 1200-1800 m rain-snow transition where SWE and melt-timing dominate partitioning; place validation columns at SNOTEL sites; avoid enumerating coordinates (downstream expander samples DEM/SSURGO).
sampling_strategy.replication: one extra column in the rain-snow transition band to capture within-band soil/aspect spread at the most sensitive elevation

sampling_plan.reason: valley/rain-dominated baseline; crosses two dominant soils to isolate texture from elevation
lower rain-snow margin; two soils to separate texture effect on early-melt partitioning
most sensitive band for SWE/melt-timing partitioning; oversampled with extra column for soil/aspect spread
snow-dominated; two soils to test texture control under deeper snowpack
peak-SWE band; anchors the top of the orographic gradient (expect low-bias SWE due to 12 km averaging)

validation_design.comparison: co-located — columns pinned to SNOTEL station cells; compare annual peak H2OSNO/SWE and melt-out timing
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE (expect ridgetop underestimation from 12 km averaging)
validation_design.n_validation_points: unknown — depends on number of SNOTEL stations in HUC 17030001

validation_design.comparison: aggregated — NOT possible natively; requires routing/aggregation of column runoff before gauge comparison

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS resolves only ~12 km; ridgetop/valley contrasts and high-elevation SWE are unresolved
single-column ELM has no lateral transport, so no integrated streamflow
needed to pin validation columns and pull observed peak SWE

requires_capabilities.capability: DEM hypsometry + SSURGO sampler for the HUC
requires_capabilities.why: expander needs elevation bands and dominant soil classes to place columns
requires_capabilities.blocks: converting strata rules into concrete points

requires_capabilities.why: columns cold-start; snow/soil states must not be init artifacts

assumptions: Domain is within CONUS so NLDAS-2 (elevation-varying) forcing applies rather than Qian T62 fallback.
SSURGO coverage exists across the HUC; 'dominant' soil classes to be resolved by the expander.
Number and elevation of SNOTEL/USGS stations in-domain unknown at design time; validation counts are data-dictated.
Baseline forcing period drawn from 1980-2018; a representative multi-year snow-season window will be selected downstream.
No lateral groundwater or column-to-column exchange is represented.
open_questions: How many SNOTEL stations fall inside HUC 17030001, and at what elevations?
Is investment in a routing/aggregation step warranted to enable USGS gauge validation?
Preferred forcing window (full 1980-2018 climatology vs specific wet/dry snow years)?
Is a full multi-year spin-up acceptable, or should the WTD-informed warm start be used to control cost?
